messages.subject: Does renjin support Big Data and how scalable it is
messages.subject_clean: Does renjin support Big Data and how scalable it is
messages.body_plain:
Hi Team,

We are trying to develop predictive Analytic tool but we want to do it on java based platform.

Then heard about Renjin. I found it very interesting.

But there is not much tutorial regarding this on google.

So I want to clarify few things  like

1.)    As Its runs on JVM then it will not have memory problem that R has? Please confirm

2.)    How much data it can process. Will it fit with big data implementation?

3.)    What sort of API it offers?

4.) How scalable it is ?

Thanks,
Chandra

Re: Does renjin support Big Data and how scalable it is
messages.subject_clean: Does renjin support Big Data and how scalable it is
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chandra,
"Big data" and "scalable" mean different things to different people :-)

I'd suggest taking a look at http://docs.renjin.org for an introduction to development with Renjin. With regard to how Renjin aims to address R's "memory problem", you might find the blog post on Renjin's Vector Pipeliner of interest:
http://www.renjin.org/blog/2013-07-30-deep-dive-vector-pipeliner.html

I'd also suggest doing your own benchmarking to verify that Renjin will meet your needs. If for any reason you find Renjin deficient in running your particular benchmarks, I'd encourage you to submit them to the renjin-benchmarks project so we can continue to improve Renjin's handling of large analysis problems.

Good luck!

Alex

messages.subject_clean: Any other license better support commercial use case?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kang,
Could you tell me a little more about what you see as problematic differences between GPLv3 and v2? I believe the choice to license Renjin under v3 was primarily driven at the time by the fact that v3 was the "latest" version of the GPL at the time of Renjin's inception.

Relicensing Renjin under GPLv2 would require tracking down our various contributors and obtaining their permission, so I think we would need to have a specific, compelling reason to do so.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: Any other license better support commercial use case?
messages.subject_clean: Any other license better support commercial use case?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

Thanks for the reply. I don't know the detail difference between v2 and v3 (Sth found here: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/41460/what-are-the-differences-between-gpl-v2-and-gpl-v3-licenses). and I'll look into it further. What I know know is GPLv3 is more restrict than v2 and industrial people don't like v3 much. I have this feeling because I used to work in Amazon and now in Apple, both of them don't like v3 (prohibit use in production). And v2 is on the boundary, kind of OK. For example, we are allowed to use old version of some other machine learning library.

R is one of the two widely used data scientist language in industry (another one is python). The advantage of R is it have better statistics support. However, integrating R into the mainstream JVM based solution is a pain because of all kinds of dependency problems. Most of of large industry company like amazon, twitter, google, apple use java dominately. Renjin is a great solution for industry because it is fully JVM implementation. I hope to integrate it with Apache Spark so we can parallel train and predict the model. I didn't find better solution to build statistics model on top of JVM than Renjin.

Currently I am experimenting on integrating Renjin and spark (there are also one open source project like https://github.com/onetapbeyond/renjin-spark-executor). If we can make use of Renjin (with a relative soft license) in our data pipeline, that would enable us to build better things.

Thanks

Kang

messages.subject: using renjin for matlab
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

We need to use some R-modules from matlab and found Renjin project as interface between Java and R. Matlab can use java modules, java can use R through renjin - profit ;) But there is a problem - matlab can use only java7 apps and when we call our minimal java project with renjin (http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/library/evaluating.html - this) from matlab it throws Runtime Exception, which may occur if there is dependenciess compiled for java 8. So my question is what last renjin version was written with only java7 behind it?

messages.subject: Re: using renjin for matlab
messages.body_plain:
Renjin *should* require only Java 7. We did drop support for Java 6 this year but I think the goal will be to support Java 7 for the next 1-2 years.

Can you open a ticket at https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues with the full stacktrace of the exception? If it is really about Java 8 than you should see something about a unknown classfile version.

Thanks for reporting and this and hope we can get it to work - would be exciting to see Renjin used in the matlab environment!

-Alex
